tier_reason: README Results table (benchmark program in the repo, `time ./benchmark <id> 12 100000`) shows modified Kraft 0.41 s vs Package-Merge 1.17 s, MiniZ 0.58 s, JPEG 0.61 s, BZip2 0.88 s, and 0.24 s vs 0.96 s at an 8-bit limit. These are first-party numbers on 'Core i7 / GCC x64' with no CPU model or flags, so not A.

corrections.caveats: Benchmark code is public but CPU model and compiler flags are missing, so tier C. One dataset (histogram of the first 64 KB of enwik). Baselines are the author's own reimplementations of Package-Merge, MiniZ/JPEG and BZip2 length limiting, not the upstream libraries run directly. Times are wall times for 100,000 repeats on the author's machine. In the length-limit table the 12-bit Strategy B time is 0.40 s (0.41 s in the main table). The author does not call the project finished; 10 commits, last one 2021-06-30 (over 3 years ago). The repo was fuzzed with afl-fuzz (Feb 2021 commit). Found through the GitHub huffman topic page, not Hacker News.

notes: Numbers and license (Zlib, Copyright 2021 Stephan Brumme) verified; 25 stars, not archived. maintenance_status changed from finished to abandoned because the README never says the project is complete and the last commit is 2021-06-30.

tier_reason: Commit 65e2abcb (Noel Gordon) states raw crc32 is 5x-25x faster than zlib's default BYFOUR crc32, gzip- and zlib-wrapped inflate are 69% and 50% faster on the snappy corpus, and PNG 140 corpus decoding is 4% faster (40% combined with adler32 SIMD and chunk copy). It gives no CPU model or flags, and its details sit on crbug.com/796178, which is blocked. The public harness third_party/zlib/contrib/bench/zlib_bench.cc exists, but the commit does not tie it to a stated CPU and flags, so first-party C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: CRC-32 5x-25x faster than zlib's default BYFOUR crc32; gzip- and zlib-wrapped inflate 69% and 50% faster on the snappy corpus; PNG 140 corpus decoding rate 4% faster on average from crc32 alone, 40% total combined with adler32 SIMD and inflate chunk copy. Later commits report gains over the previous Chromium zlib, not upstream: the ANZAC++ hash gives 30-40% faster compression (M1 31.3%, SPR 41.9%; 0.1% ratio loss on snappy) and overlapped bitstream refill gives an 8.09% average inflate gain across 7 CPUs (EPYC 9B45 7.86%, EPYC 9B14 11.21%, Xeon 8481C 6.16%, Axion 8.89%, Ryzen 9 9900X 8.77%, Cortex-X3 5.53%, Cortex-X4 10.13%).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: SSE4.2 and PCLMUL for the SIMD crc32 code (selected at run time); since Aug 2026 the SIMD ISA is set per function via __target__. Benchmark compiler and flags not stated in the commits.
corrections.caveats: Headline numbers come from a first-party commit message (the 2018 SSE4.2 crc32 change) with no CPU model, compiler or flags; its details are on crbug.com/796178, which was blocked here. Newer commits (ANZAC++ hash 2023, bitstream-refill overlap 2026-09-22) name CPUs but measure against the previous Chromium zlib, not upstream madler/zlib, and do not state the tool or flags. A public harness exists at third_party/zlib/contrib/bench/zlib_bench.cc. This is a distinct fork from Cloudflare zlib (an independent fork) and zlib-ng (a separate project that adopted some Chromium ideas such as chunk copy), with its own code (*simd* files, contrib/optimizations) and its own evidence, so it is not a duplicate. The repo URL is the whole Chromium mirror; the code is in third_party/zlib (canonical: chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/third_party/zlib). Synced to zlib 1.3.2.

notes: Kept as a distinct fork: it has its own SIMD crc32/adler32, chunk-copy inflate and ANZAC++ hash, its own commit evidence, and still ships in Chrome. License Zlib per README.chromium; last commit 2026-09-22 verified. The 24.9k-star figure for the mirror was not rechecked. Consider pointing repo_url at https://github.com/chromium/chromium/tree/main/third_party/zlib.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 38 stars; compression backend of the png crate; 175.7M all-time crates.io downloads (58.1M recent)
corrections.caveats: No numbers could be read: the only data is a plot image in discussion #68 (blocked here), which the author calls very preliminary, and its compared libraries are not named in text. The benchmark harness is the separate fintelia/corpus-bench repo; no CPU or compiler stated. Baselines are zlib-rs and zlib-ng, not upstream zlib directly. Only levels 1-7 are implemented (8-9 missing). Rust only; not callable from C++ without writing a binding. Latest crates.io release is 0.3.7 (2024-12); the compressor work on main is unreleased. Re-tier to C if someone reads the plot values.

notes: Downgraded C to D because the numbers could not be checked. Not rejected: it is notable through use (png crate backend, about 176M crates.io downloads). zlib-ng is already catalogued, so baseline_in_list is true. License MIT OR Apache-2.0 and last commit 2026-05-31 verified.
